summary: Frontier legend Jim Bowie, namesake of the Bowie knife, ran a slave-smuggling scam with pirate Jean Lafitte, forged vast land claims in Louisiana and Arkansas, raided Native peoples in Texas, and died at the Alamo in 1836.

evidence.note: birth in Logan County, Kentucky, in 1796, date hedged as approximate
Bowie brothers buy Lafitte's captives and game the informer bounty to launder them
Bowie personally marches chained captives through the swamps, ruling by fear
joins the 1819 Long filibuster expedition into Spanish Texas
close account of the Sandbar Fight ending with Bowie disembowelling Norris Wright
family markets the Bowie knife as a brand; knife spreads nationwide
scale of forged land claims in Arkansas and Louisiana
silver-hunting incursion and multi-day fight with Tawakoni, Waco and Caddo people
Bowie's men repeatedly hang and burn a captured Mexican man for information
bedridden with illness when the Alamo falls in 1836; rival death legends reviewed

notes: Primary theme folklore-legend because the series frames Bowie as the real figure behind a Texas school legend; fraud-grift or slavery-forced-labor would be defensible. Texas events map to US; the brief Monclova (Coahuila) episode was too short to add MX. Both Louisiana and Texas are central, so both subdivisions are listed. Lafitte's birth and death years are uncertain, so floruit is used. Roles: Texian revolutionary army is not quite a state force.
